verdict.rationale: PayPal documents registrable outbound HTTPS webhooks: up to 10 URLs per app, filtered by event type, retried up to 25 times over 3 days, with a signature-verification endpoint. The REST overview places Webhook events on the same rails the Agent Toolkit calls. However, nothing ties these webhooks to the agentic-commerce surface, such as event types for agent-initiated carts, Store Sync orders, or ACP/UCP checkout sessions. Missing for 10: documented agentic-commerce-specific webhook event types (cart/checkout/agent-order events), evidence that Store Sync, Agent Ready or cart flows emit subscribable events, independent or hands-on corroboration of webhook delivery.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Webhooks are HTTPS posts from PayPal to an endpoint on your server whenever the corresponding event type occurs
Up to 10 webhook URLs may be subscribed per app
Any non-2xx status code will cause PayPal to reattempt delivery up to 25 times over the course of 3 days or until it receives a 2xx success code.
Webhook events references — the same rails the Agent Toolkit's tools call
